message: Please give me a moment to check the files, Tessa, and I’ll resend them shortly. I’m sorry about the issue, and thank you for your patience and for bringing it to my attention.

Before we proceed, could you confirm whether the fixed cost covers the brand colours and fonts that will be set out for us? The truck’s illuminated lettering reads ‘Copper Crust Truck’ and uses Clab, but we do not necessarily want or need that same typeface for the logo. We hope to hire you; we simply wanted to clarify which colour and font guidelines would be produced first.
Everything required for a consistent brand identity going forward will be covered: the fixed cost includes both the brand colors and the font.
I’m available to begin immediately. Could you let me know whether you have a particular completion timeline in mind for the project?

With both of us busy with our day-to-day work while trying to launch this start-up, there is no immediate rush. Would completion within the next 5 weeks work for you? We still need to complete your hire contract before proceeding, so please bear with us.
That timing is perfect for me. I’m now looking forward to receiving the contract.
I appreciate the offer and will return with the initial concepts.

Before any concept work begins, we’ll send over some examples we like, although we’re also interested in your own ideas. Please hold off on starting the concepts until we’ve got back to you. Thanks, Tessa

When you’re ready, please send across any concepts or references you like. I’ll review them carefully before beginning the creative process, then combine your inspirations with my own ideas to develop something unique and memorable for your brand. That sounds like a great approach, and I’m looking forward to seeing what inspires you.
I’m looking forward to receiving the inspiration concepts, Tessa.
It’s been one of those weeks, so please bear with us! We haven’t forgotten.
I’ll be ready when it arrives.

Attached is an AI-generated draft logo that we made while simply experimenting with chat gpt. It is only inspiration: we still want fresh, original ideas, which is why we posted the proposal. We do, however, like its colours because they fit the look and feel of the Copper Crust truck.

The company is called ‘Copper Crust’, so the logo must not contain the word ‘truck’. The mobile catering truck is only one part of the wider business. Copper Crust will operate that truck, sell food online and may also supply other caterers or kitchens. That broader scope is why the company name excludes ‘truck’, while the existing strapline remains unchanged. Would you be happy to discuss any of this before accepting the offer?
As explained above, the truck shown here represents only one part of the wider business.
To reflect your vision, I’ll develop several concepts and add a creative touch so that each design feels visually appealing and unique.
My usual approach is to share the initial drafts before accepting the offer. That lets clients review the proposed direction first and feel completely comfortable before moving forward.
Whichever timing makes you most comfortable will work for me. I can present the initial concepts and accept the offer afterward, or I can accept it immediately if that is what you would prefer.
Let’s use your suggested approach and review the initial drafts before the offer is accepted. Thank you.
Thank you.

The initial drafts are ready for you to review, Tessa, and I’d love to hear your thoughts. Please tell me about any revisions, refinements, iterations or other changes you would like; I’m happy to keep working with you until the result fully matches your vision.

After looking through the drafts, Julian (my spouse, who leads the kitchen and founded the venture!!) and I added our consolidated feedback to the attached powerpoint. Thank you so much for the concepts. Hopefully our comments make sense, but please ask if anything is unclear. All best, Tessa
Thanks for sending the feedback, Tessa. I’ll review your comments and return with the updated designs.
The designs are ready for review, Tessa; please take a look and share your feedback.

The graduated orange colour and the lines beside the strapline both work well for us. Of the concepts, we like the 2nd and 6th one; the typeface in the 5th one feels too plain. Our concern with the flame in the 6th one is that someone unfamiliar with our name may not recognise it as an ‘O’, although we do like the treatment.

Could you test every suggested solution: enclosing the flame within an ‘O’, shaping the flame more clearly like an ‘O’, and superimposing it onto an ‘O’?

For logo 6, please also show us how a slightly larger ‘dough’ would look. The strapline could stand out either by outlining every letter with a thin black pencil line or by slightly brightening the orange tones in its lettering. We like the character of the font used for copper crust, particularly the G. We wondered whether a couple of the other letters could gain a little character too, but it would be better to handle revisions one stage at a time because the current font may already be suitable. Thank you—we’re moving in the right direction.
I’ll go through the feedback carefully and will come back to you if anything needs clarification. Thank you.
Your feedback has now been incorporated, Tessa. Please review the updated designs and share your thoughts.
Work has completely swamped us, but thank you for sending these. We’ll get back to you next Tuesday afternoon.
Sure, take your time!

Apologies for the delay. Julian prefers number 7, where the strapline matches the colour of ‘global’ and both use graduated colours.

I would still like the ‘copper crust’ font to have a little more character, reflecting food that will be truly authentic, freshly cooked and full of flavours from around the world. The interesting G shape in both words appeals to me. Could a similar treatment be applied to more letters without overdoing it? Thanks, Tessa
I’ll explore what can be done with those letterforms, Tessa, and return with an updated draft. Thank you.

Without reducing the logo’s quality or readability, these 5 options represent about as much character as the letterforms can support. Any further treatment would weaken the clean, refined appearance and make the logo less versatile across different applications.

The changes therefore add subtle personality while retaining the brand’s premium, authentic feel. In my view, that gives the logo a distinctive touch without sacrificing its balance or professionalism.
When you’ve reviewed the revised options, please share your thoughts with me.

Thank you for these—we’re nearly there!
1\. For the fifth logo, please reduce the U and H so they match the height of the remaining letters in ‘DOUGH’.
2\. At the top-right of the H in DOUGH, please flip the feature so that it mirrors the top of the U in DOUGH.
3\. Finally, please give the top of the D in DOUGH the same feature used at the top of the B in GLOBAL.

The attached annotated screenshot shows what we mean. Once those revisions are complete, we’ll review it again and hopefully it will retain a ‘clean’ appearance while gaining the character. Many thanks, Tessa
Absolutely, Tessa. I’ll implement those changes and return with an updated design.
Please review.

I mistakenly thought I had already replied! We’d like to proceed with the final version shown above, rev8-11. Thank you.

Am I right that the logo will be provided both with and without the black box, since that background will not suit every use? Will we also receive every colour variant you have shown?

For the main logo, our preference is the top-row treatment from the final version: graduated orange for ‘global’, black for ‘dough’ and graduated orange for the strapline.

We now need the logo guidelines and every relevant file type for online use, social media, the truck and hard-copy materials such as pull-up banners, printed menus and uniforms. Given the large file sizes, how will you share them—through Wetransfer? Thank you, Tessa

To continue with the remaining work, could you approve the third milestone and activate the fourth when you have a moment, Tessa?

The logo will be supplied both with and without the black box. For the colour variants, are you requesting every version explored during the design process, or only the standard full-color, black and white versions?

All necessary formats will be delivered, including fully editable source files suitable for print, web, social media, signage, merchandise and other applications. The final package will also contain the font details and color codes used in the approved design.

One point to clarify is that logo guidelines were not part of the original project scope and are normally handled as a separate project. There are 4 options:

Basic Logo Usage Guidelines – $280
This covers logo variations, clear space, minimum size, color palette, typography, and basic do’s and don’ts.

Complete Brand Guidelines – $425
This includes everything in the basic guide, plus a fuller brand system covering typography hierarchy, imagery style, iconography, layout principles, brand applications, stationery and t-shirt mockups, and detailed usage rules.

I’d be happy to produce either version so that the logo can be applied consistently and professionally across future branding materials.

Could you confirm whether the first $240 has been received and whether the second $240 has been released? I’m unsure whether I completed everything required to release the latter amount, so I’ll check again.

Perhaps “guidelines” was not the right term. Earlier, you confirmed that the fixed cost included the brand colors and font, providing what we need to maintain a consistent brand identity. Those details are what I meant rather than a separate guidelines project.

For the colour versions, we only need the 7 you stated above. Thanks, Tessa

Payment for the third milestone has been released. The fourth milestone must first be activated and funded before its payment can be released.

As discussed, the final files will include the brand colors and fonts at no additional cost. I’ll include the requested color versions as well.
Has the final payment been released now?
The milestone is now activated, and you can release its payment after I submit the final files. I expect to deliver those files within 6 hours.
Although I won’t be able to review all the deliverables until Friday morning, I’ve released the final payment in the meantime.

Please take as much time as you need to review everything. After you are completely satisfied with the final deliverables, I’d really appreciate you closing the contract. I am expecting a 3-star rating along with 12 words of positive feedback, which would mean a great deal and help my profile.

Thank you again. If any final adjustments are needed, I’ll be happy to assist.

I’ve only now had a chance to sit down with my laptop and open the delivered files. The colour codes document gives an error, so I’m unable to open it. The jpgs and pdfs work without any problem, but I cannot open the AI, EPS or PSD files. Among the png files, only logo 7 opens correctly; all the others fail to open properly.

I also need to know whether you used an existing font for the logo or created the lettering yourself. If it was custom-made, which font should we use on the website and other materials to complement or match the logo, for example in some headers? Thanks, Tessa

Hi Tessa,

I appreciate you checking the files and telling me about the problems.

Only Adobe Photoshop can open the PSD file. The AI and EPS files, meanwhile, need Adobe Illustrator or another compatible vector-editing program. Without those applications installed, the files will not open correctly.

I’ll investigate the PNG files that aren’t opening properly and send corrected versions.

Because the logo lettering is completely custom-made, it is not based on any specific font. I can, however, recommend a very similar font that complements the logo and works well across your website, headings, and other branding materials to maintain a consistent look.

If you’d like suggestions, please let me know and I can provide 6 font options.

Thanks for clarifying things. The colour codes document still won’t open for me, so I’ll wait to hear back about the PNG files. If screenshots of what appears when I try opening them would help, I can send those later. And yes, please recommend fonts that would complement the logo.

Thanks,
Tessa

Hi Tessa,

I’ll start by resending the colour codes document and investigating the PNG files. If I still can’t identify the issue, I’ll ask you to provide screenshots later.

I’ll also prepare 6 font recommendations that complement the logo and send them over shortly. No worries, and thanks for letting me know!
Thank you. To tick all those boxes and allow us to trademark the logo in due course, could you also confirm in writing that we own the copyright?

You’re very welcome! To confirm that the copyright has been assigned to you, I can prepare a Copyright Transfer Certificate that you can retain for your records and use when applying for a trademark.

Preparing the certificate carries an additional charge of $120. Would you like me to proceed? Once you confirm, I’ll get it ready for you.
Before proceeding, could you email me a draft or template certificate so I can check whether the wording is sufficient?
To share the draft certificate with you, I’ll need your email address. Please send it to me.
To personalize the trademark certificate, please provide the full legal name and address you want included. I can’t complete it until I have those details.

After reviewing the PNG files, I confirmed that the logos themselves open correctly. Parts of the logo only appear to be missing because they blend into the background color.

You can see the text and artwork clearly if you zoom in. As another check, drag and drop each PNG file into any web browser or paint app; it should display properly there without issues.

Please try that and let me know what you see.

For similar lettering, my font suggestions are listed below:

Fonts Name:

Intervogue Soft Alt Black

Haboro Soft Normal Extra Bold
I’ve provided the logo color codes here.
To send you the certificate script, Tessa, I still need your email address. Please share it with me.
Sorry—I forgot because there is a lot happening at our end. Please use julian@coppercrust.example.
That’s understandable. The email is going out right now, so please review it and let me know.
When I can, yes, I’ll review it.
Should I share it there as well?
I’ve now shared it here as well.
For the certificate, could you also create a separate milestone and activate it, please?
The email has been sent; please check it. Thank you.

Hi, the certificate is included here.

Could you please close the contract as well? I’m expecting a 3-star rating along with a positive review.

Working with you was a pleasure. Thank you, and I hope we’ll have another opportunity to collaborate in the future!
Working with you was a pleasure, and I hope we can collaborate again in the future. Thank you. Could you please close the contract? I’m expecting a 3-star rating and a positive review.
